coordination_scope.qwen_core_current_work: mixed streaming preamble + tool-call durable restart checkpoint
coordination_scope.qwen_reliability_current_work: request-wide bounded failover budget and local provider-preparation accounting
coordination_scope.why_this_is_independent: This finding is request concurrency for one logical OpenAI session across Core durability and Reliability admission; it does not alter current mixed-turn serialization or account candidate ordering.

product_observations: server.js reads sessionStore.getRecord(sessionKey), computes restoredMessages and checks pending tool calls before an asynchronous provider request.
There is no per-session admission/serialization gate around /v1/chat/completions; request-governor allows bounded concurrent upstream work per account rather than serializing a logical conversation.
sessionStore.set() rejects only the narrow same-chat-id/different-account mismatch. Two same-account writers with different fresh chat ids are both accepted and each can replace durable history.

For two simultaneous short continuation requests, both can observe zero pending tool calls before either accepted tool-call is checkpointed. Both can therefore reach Qwen and both accepted tool calls can be released to clients.
The later sessionStore.set() replaces history from the earlier writer. One already-released mutating tool call can disappear from durable pending-call state.
risk: Two concurrent retries/continue deliveries for one OpenCode/OpenAI session can create two model turns and two mutating tool calls from the same pre-state.
One accepted call can be forgotten by the durable checkpoint even though it was already returned to a client and may have executed locally.
After restart, the pending-tool guard can only protect the surviving checkpoint and cannot reconcile the forgotten accepted call.
Fresh upstream chat/account affinity for the same logical session becomes last-writer-wins.
minimal_product_contract: Serialize admission/execution by canonical sessionKey for /v1/chat/completions; unrelated session keys must remain concurrent.
A queued same-session continuation must re-read durable state after acquiring the gate. If an accepted tool-call is pending, it must fail before provider work with QWEN_PENDING_TOOL_RESULT.

The gate must cover the interval from durable pre-state read through accepted assistant-turn checkpoint/client release boundary. Holding it for the full request is the simplest safe first implementation.
Release must be guaranteed on response finish/close/error/cancellation.
Add a regression with two simultaneous same-session continue requests proving provider_calls=1 and released_mutating_calls=1; add a control proving different sessions remain concurrent.
limits: Semantic offline harness models the exact relevant server/session-store ordering; full private repository tree was not executed locally.
No hosted CI, Cloudflare, live Qwen/Notion/Codex, Windows, production, real user data or secrets used.
